UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

Plaintiff,  v.  KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6,

Defendants. ____________________________________/

Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

[PROPOSED] ORDER B

This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff’s Rule 54(b) Motion to Reconsider ECF No. 108 as to ECF No. 103 (ECF No. ___). Upon consideration of the Motion, the Memorandum in Support, any response and reply, and the record, it is hereby

ORDERED that the Motion is GRANTED IN PART to the extent stated in this Order. The Order signed October 29, 2026 and entered October 30, 2026 (ECF No. 108) is MODIFIED insofar as it denied Plaintiff’s Motion for Entry of a Scheduling Order and, as Necessary, an Initial Pretrial Conference (ECF No. 103), to the extent stated below. This Order acts on ECF No. 103. It does not reconsider the disposition of ECF No. 105 in ECF No. 108; and it is

FURTHER ORDERED that the determination stated in ECF No. 108 that discovery will not begin until resolution of the pending motions to dismiss (ECF Nos. 10, 21, 45) implements the following operative direction of the District Judge, with its date and operative terms, the undersigned’s own case-management determination on the present record, or both, stated to the extent necessary to determine the scheduling obligations in this action and the scope of the authority referred to the undersigned: ______________________________________________; and it is

FURTHER ORDERED that the direction or determination identified in the preceding paragraph applies to entry of the scheduling order under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16(b) as follows: ______________________________________________; and applies to an initial scheduling conference under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16(b)(1)(B) and Local Civil Rule 16(B) as follows: ______________________________________________; and it is

FURTHER ORDERED that the Court’s basis for continuing to postpone each of the following steps is stated here or in an accompanying memorandum opinion: (a) entry of the scheduling order, under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16(b)(2): ______________________________________________; and (b) the initial scheduling conference: ______________________________________________; and it is

FURTHER ORDERED that, within fourteen (14) days after disposition of the last of ECF Nos. 10, 21, and 45, if the action remains pending, the Court will establish the next scheduling step by one of the following: (a) entering a scheduling order under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 16(b)(3) upon receipt of a sufficient report under Rule 26(f); (b) setting a scheduling conference under Rule 16(b)(1)(B); or (c) directing a procedure that accounts for any leave to amend granted in the disposition. The Court may establish the next scheduling step earlier, after disposition of any one of those motions, where that disposition permits scheduling to proceed as to any party or claim. No further motion by any party is required to obtain the step this paragraph provides; and it is

FURTHER ORDERED that, except as expressly stated in this Order, this Order does not modify any other order of the Court and does not resolve any objection or motion pending before the District Judge.

The Clerk’s Office is directed to provide a copy of this Order to pro se Plaintiff at his last known address.

It is SO ORDERED.

Alexandria, Virginia

__________, 2026

______________________________

William E. Fitzpatrick

United States Magistrate Judge
